1.e4 d6 2.d4 Nf6 3.Nc3 e5 4.Nf3 Nbd7 5.B.strategy: Castles before committing the centre, so White can meet whatever Black chooses. The position has no quick break against Black's solid set-up, and the game becomes a manoeuvring fight over the tension on d4 and e5: space against solidity.

Completes a compact set-up around e5: pawn on d6, knights on d7 and f6, bishop on e7. The pawn on c6 takes b5 and d5 away from White's pieces, so Black keeps a firm grip on e5 and can wait, at the cost of space.
1.e4 d6 2.d4 Nf6 3.Nc3 e5 4.Nf3 Nbd7 5.B.name: Philidor Defence: Lion Variation, Lion's Claw, with Be2 and c6
